title: Perf Regression Canary – Alert Policy (p95 latency + tokens/sec)
author: Sean Gallagher
body:
## Purpose
This page defines how we alert on performance regressions detected by the **Perf Regression Canary** in production. The goal is to:
- Detect **tail latency (p95)** and **throughput (tokens/sec)** regressions early, per model and critical slices.
- Page only when action is required and signal quality is high (avoid pager fatigue).
- Ensure alerts contain enough context to triage quickly (runtime build, kernel selection, scheduler mode, GPU SKU, batch stats).
- Make routing between **SRE** and **Serving Runtime** predictable.

This policy applies to **canary-generated traffic only** (request tag `source=perf-canary`). It does not change customer-facing SLO alerting.

---

## Definitions (what we alert on)
We alert on two primary signals computed from canary metrics:
1) **Latency regression**: increase in end-to-end request latency p95 (ms), split by model and slice.
2) **Throughput regression**: decrease in effective tokens/sec (t/s) p50 and p95 (depending on workload mode), split by model and slice.

**Key slices (dimensions)**
Per the metric spec and cardinality budget, alerts may be emitted only for the following label set:
- `model` (canonical model id)
- `region` (e.g., `us-east`, `eu-west`)
- `gpu_sku` (coarse SKU: `a100-80g`, `h100-80g`, etc.)
- `scheduler_mode` (enumerated set only; no free-form)
- `runtime_build` (short build id) and `runtime_git_sha` (short SHA) included in alert payload (not required for grouping)

**Modes covered**
- Streaming and non-streaming
- Prefill+decode workload shapes defined in the workload matrix

---

## Baseline strategy (what we compare against)
Baseline strategy is defined in **ADR-0231**. In short:
- Default: **rolling baseline** = median of the same slice over the last **7 days** (excluding suppression windows and warmup).
- Optional: **pinned known-good baseline** for high-risk rollouts or when rolling baseline is unstable for a slice.

**Baseline selection rules**
- Use rolling 7d median when we have sufficient historical data (>= 4 distinct days with valid sample windows).
- Fall back to pinned known-good when:
  - new slice is introduced (new model, new GPU SKU, new scheduler mode), or
  - rolling baseline variance exceeds the noise budget, or
  - we are in an active runtime release candidate window.

---

## Alert classes and actions
We distinguish between **paging** and **ticketing** based on severity, confidence, and blast radius.

### Severity mapping
| Severity | Delivery | Intended response | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEV-2 | Page (PagerDuty) | Immediate triage (SRE), fast mitigation/rollback if confirmed | p95 latency up materially in a region + model slice on active runtime build |
| SEV-3 | Page or ticket (see rules below) | Investigate within business hours unless ongoing customer impact is suspected | tokens/sec down moderately; stable repro across windows |
| SEV-4 | Ticket only | Track and fix without oncall interruption | single-slice regression close to threshold; suspected noise |

**General principle:** page only when (a) regression is sustained, (b) sample size is adequate, and (c) effect size exceeds a meaningful threshold.

---

## Thresholds (v1)
Thresholds are intentionally conservative in phase 1 and will be tuned with backtesting results.

### 1) Latency p95 regression thresholds
Trigger condition is evaluated per slice (model/region/gpu_sku/scheduler_mode) over an evaluation window.

**SEV-2 (page)**
- Condition: `p95_latency_ms` is **>= +20%** versus baseline
- AND absolute delta is **>= +40 ms**
- Sustained for **3 of 4** consecutive **10-minute** windows (i.e., ~30 minutes sustained)
- AND minimum canary volume: **>= 300 requests** total across the evaluated 40 minutes for that slice

**SEV-3 (ticket, or page during release windows)**
- Condition: `p95_latency_ms` is **>= +12%** versus baseline
- AND absolute delta is **>= +25 ms**
- Sustained for **4 of 6** consecutive **10-minute** windows (~40 minutes)
- AND minimum canary volume: **>= 500 requests**
- Delivery: ticket by default; **page** if (a) current runtime build is in “release candidate” channel, or (b) the regression is present in **>=2 regions** for the same model.

### 2) Tokens/sec regression thresholds
Tokens/sec regressions are more sensitive to batching/scheduler effects; we apply stricter noise controls.

**SEV-2 (page)**
- Condition: `tokens_per_sec` is **<= -15%** versus baseline
- Sustained for **3 of 4** consecutive **10-minute** windows
- AND minimum canary volume: **>= 200 streaming sessions** OR **>= 400 non-streaming requests** (depending on mode)

**SEV-3 (ticket)**
- Condition: `tokens_per_sec` is **<= -10%** versus baseline
- Sustained for **4 of 6** consecutive **10-minute** windows
- AND minimum volume as above

### 3) Guardrails (do not alert)
To reduce false positives, the detector MUST suppress alerts when:
- Warmup period is active (see “Warmup & cache priming suppression”).
- The slice has insufficient volume (below minimums above).
- The baseline is missing or marked “unstable” by the detector.
- The slice is in a declared maintenance window (regional rollout, fleet rebalancing, GPU driver change).

---

## Paging vs ticketing rules (delivery policy)
### Paging (PagerDuty)
We page only for SEV-2 conditions and the SEV-3 escalation cases defined above.

PagerDuty service: **Perf Canary – Regressions**
- Primary: **SRE Oncall**
- Secondary/escalation: **Serving Runtime Oncall**

### Ticketing (Linear)
All alert firings (including pages) should create a Linear issue in the “Perf Canary” project for traceability.
- SEV-2: ticket created automatically and linked in the PD incident
- SEV-3/SEV-4: ticket only (unless SEV-3 escalates to page)

Ticket template must include:
- slice (model/region/gpu_sku/scheduler_mode)
- metric regressed (p95 latency vs tokens/sec)
- baseline type (rolling vs pinned)
- regression magnitude and time window
- links: Grafana dashboard, deploy annotations, runbook

---

## Alert grouping & deduplication
### Grouping intent
A single root cause (e.g., one runtime build) can cause multiple slice regressions. We want:
- Enough grouping to avoid a paging storm
- Enough separation to keep signal actionable (model/region-specific regressions matter)

### Dedup key (PagerDuty)
Dedup key format (must remain stable):
`perf-canary|<metric>|<model>|<region>|<gpu_sku>|<scheduler_mode>`

Notes:
- `runtime_build` is intentionally NOT part of the PD dedup key to avoid multiple incidents during rollout churn.
- The alert payload MUST include `runtime_build` and `runtime_git_sha` so responders can correlate with deploy annotations.

### Grouping rules
- Page at most **one incident per slice per metric** within a 2-hour period.
- If multiple slices for the same model/region regress simultaneously:
  - prefer a single page per metric per model/region with the top 3 impacted GPU SKUs summarized in the alert body
  - open separate tickets for each affected slice

### Auto-resolve policy
- Auto-resolve only after the metric returns to within **+5%** (latency) / **-5%** (tokens/sec) of baseline for **3 consecutive 10-minute windows**.
- If suppression is active (maintenance), do not auto-resolve; mark as “suppressed” and rely on maintenance end.

---

## Maintenance windows & suppression
We support three suppression mechanisms.

### 1) Deploy-window suppression (automatic)
When a runtime deploy annotation is detected for a region:
- suppress alerts for the affected region for **15 minutes**
- then re-enable but require **one additional evaluation window** (effectively +10 minutes) before paging

Rationale: avoids paging during cache priming + initial fleet rebalancing.

### 2) Warmup & cache priming suppression (automatic)
The canary runner performs warmup/priming steps for each slice.
- suppress alert evaluation for the first **N warmup runs** (per workload matrix; default N=3)
- suppress the first **10 minutes** after a slice becomes active (new model, new GPU SKU)

### 3) Manual maintenance windows (operator-driven)
SRE may declare a manual maintenance window for known disruptive events (driver rollouts, cluster evacuation, large-scale autoscaler tuning).
- Scope: region and optionally GPU SKU
- Maximum duration: 6 hours (extend requires approval by SRE lead)
- Must be communicated in `#eng-oncall` with reason and expected end time

**Important:** manual maintenance windows should be the exception; do not use them to hide legitimate regressions.

---

## Oncall routing and responsibilities
### Ownership model
- **SRE Oncall** owns initial triage for all perf-canary pages (signal quality, infra correlation, suppression correctness).
- **Serving Runtime Oncall** owns confirmed runtime regressions (kernel selection changes, scheduler changes, runtime build issues).

### Routing steps (SEV-2 page)
1) Page goes to **SRE Oncall** with runbook link.
2) SRE validates:
   - sample size met
   - not within suppression window
   - regression is not explained by known infra event
3) If confirmed and likely runtime-related:
   - SRE engages **Serving Runtime Oncall** (PagerDuty add-responder) and posts summary in `#eng-runtime`.
4) If customer impact is suspected (based on separate customer SLO alerts or support signal), follow standard incident process.

### When to engage Runtime immediately (skip extended SRE validation)
- Regression is correlated with a runtime deploy annotation and exceeds SEV-2 threshold
- Regression is present across **>=2 regions** for the same model
- Alert payload shows a kernel fallback reason or scheduler mode change from baseline

---

## Alert payload requirements (must include)
Every page/ticket must include the following fields:
- Model, region, GPU SKU, scheduler mode
- Metric (p95 latency or tokens/sec) and regression magnitude (% and absolute)
- Baseline type (rolling 7d vs pinned) and baseline value
- Time range of evaluation and number of windows violated
- Canary volume (requests/sessions) and any “data quality” flags
- Current `runtime_build` and `runtime_git_sha`
- Kernel selection summary: selected kernel id, fallback reason (if any)
- Batch stats summary: prefill/decode mix, max seq len observed, mean batch size
- Links:
  - Grafana dashboard (pre-filtered to slice)
  - Deploy annotations view (runtime release timeline)
  - Runbook: /eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-perf-canary-regression-triage
  - Debug playbook: /eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/perf-regression-debug-playbook

---

## Post-alert hygiene and review
### Required follow-ups
- For every SEV-2 page: create/ensure a Linear ticket exists with root cause and mitigation decision.
- If a page is deemed false positive:
  - tag the ticket `false-positive`
  - document which guardrail failed (sample size, suppression window, baseline instability, cardinality/label issue)
  - file a tuning task against the detector (do not “just ignore it”)

### Weekly review (during rollout)
During phase 1/2 rollout, SRE + Runtime + Telemetry will review:
- number of pages and tickets
- top causes of noise
- threshold adjustments and suppression changes
- slices with unstable baselines

Owner: **Tomáš Novák** (paging hygiene), with Runtime input from **Noah Patel**.

---

## Change management
Changes to this policy require:
- Review from **SRE lead (Sean Gallagher)**
- Review from **Runtime sponsor (Mateo Alvarez)**
- Confirmation from **Telemetry/Observability** that label schema and aggregation cost remain within budget

Major changes (thresholds, dedup keys, suppression semantics) should be recorded as a short decision note linked from this page.

---

## Appendix A: Example alert (SEV-2 latency)
**Title:** `Perf Canary p95 latency regression | model=rw-llama3-70b | region=eu-west | gpu_sku=h100-80g | scheduler_mode=stable`

**Body (excerpt):**
- p95 latency: 412 ms (baseline 325 ms) **(+26.8%, +87 ms)**
- Sustained: 3/4 windows (10m) | volume: 380 requests
- runtime_build: `rt-1.18.0-rc3` | git_sha: `a1b2c3d`
- kernel: `attn_fused_v17` (fallback: none)
- batch: mean=7.2 | max_seq_len=4096 | prefill/decode=1/6
- Links: Grafana slice, deploy annotations, runbook
